samples.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four panels of equal size standing side by side, counted from the left. Every panel contains exactly three straight lines, one red, one green and one blue, and each line is drawn all the way across its own panel. Inside a panel every pair of lines crosses exactly once, so each panel shows three crossing points. In exactly one panel the three lines all run through one single common point, so its three crossings coincide and no triangle is visible there. In every other panel the three crossings stay apart and leave a small open triangle of white background between them. The same three colours, the same stroke width and three full-width lines appear in every panel, and the line bearings, the crossing location inside the panel and the size of each triangle are drawn independently of the answer, so colour, ink, line angle, crossing position and panel position carry no information. Judge each panel only by the three lines drawn inside it. Which half of the image contains the panel whose three lines all run through one common point, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
